en: Boys du Severe at Ultimatum Festival 1985-05-03
Boys du Severe at Ultimatum Festival 1985-05-03

The following is a transcription of Boys du Severe's performance at the Ultimatum Festival I, Friday, May 3rd, 1985 at the Foufounes Electriques bar and performance space in Montreal. The band is made up of Jean-Luc Bonspiel, Jean-Martin Mignault, and Josee Thibeault. Boris Wanowitch joined this specific performance, and they named the collaboration "Misère Plus." Alan Lorde joined the band's performance for the song "The Wrong Way." In Alan Lord’s memoir High Friends in Low Places (2022), Lord reflects on "Misere Plus":  "Boris Wanowitch and Boys du Sévère's production Misere Plus, with Boris and the luscious Josée Thibeault wearing those ridiculous shiny black Spanish Guardia Civil hats, sitting at an inquisitorial desk with Bonspiel, taking turns reading an amazing text being printed randomly live on a scritchy dot-matrix printer, using my cut-ups program...Boris sat in a chair reading a paper while Josée gave him a haircut, with the buzzing electric clipper amplified by mikes..." (129).

The Montreal band Boys du Sévère consisted of singer and composer Jean-Luc Bonspiel, singer Josée Thibeault, with Jean-Martin Mignault on electronic drums. They were the musical part of Boris Wanowitch and the band members’ production Misère Plus.

Boris sat at an inquisitorial desk with Jean-Luc Bonspiel, each taking turns reading from text being printed randomly live on a scritchy dot-matrix printer, using my computer cut-ups program. This was the most cutting-edge literary event of the festival, technically speaking.
Boris then sat in a chair reading a newspaper while Josée gave him a haircut, with the loud buzzing electric clipper amplified by contact mics.
Boris and singer Josée Thibeault were wearing shiny black Spanish Guardia Civil hats.
Their sacrilegious song “Jésus” was included on the festival’s documentary LP.
Festival participants Jean-Luc Bonspiel, Jean-Martin Mignault, Jack V and I later formed Montreal’s seminal agitrock band Vent du Mont Schärr (1986 – 1990).
I joined them on guitar to play the jazz chords of our old Electro-Luxe song “The Wrong Way”, this time featuring Josée’s honeydripping voice.
All of us present on stage were once Neoists - a wacky Montreal gang of exquisite troublemakers
